option_1_call_only.training_target: complete and unchanged in kind: every Stage-3 document is ONE assistant turn (prompt = system + tools + the first user turn, target = the teacher's own reply up to its <|im_end|>); a call-only episode yields exactly the document the first turn of a full episode yields, naturally terminated, teacher-native (generated from the first user turn, as every Pivot task)
option_1_call_only.gold: deterministic: the single step's call name and arguments, compared exactly after canonicalization (tool_calls.step_matches_gold), as today
option_1_call_only.verification: protocol + schema validity + step gold; recorded_execution and task_success stay None (no recorded response exists: nothing is replayed or executed, and none is claimed). Weaker than today's Pivot episodes by recorded execution only
option_1_call_only.what_it_is: a tool-call decision sample -- the right call with the right arguments at step one -- never a completed task: no tool result, no final answer; it must be recorded as its own episode shape and verification-level combination, and never counted or reported as task success
option_1_call_only.calibration_and_state_eval: one item per episode (the call turn), counted in the category's scored positions like any turn's; state_eval_hybrid@v2's schema_arguments category would mix call-only and full-episode items, so its items and its measurement protocol identity change -- it is not frozen yet, no historical identity is touched
option_1_call_only.stage3_token_counting: unchanged: unique supervised tokens of the call turn, counted before packing as tool-calling tokens
option_1_call_only.protocol_and_identity: needs, after approval: a task shape that ends on a call with no response (e.g. final_check kind ends_on_call), verify_episode accepting it only for tasks that declare it, the converter rule, a new pool content identity and a rebuilt plan, the tool-calling item version bumped (tool_calling@v1 -> v2) so measurement identities name the shape
option_1_call_only.cost: $0 code (converter rule, the verify rule, tests); generation inside the hybrid session's existing rounds: ~1,140 non-thinking tasks at the expected pass rate (~1.7 attempts each, first prompts median 2,961 tokens) ~ 5.8M prefill + 0.1M decode tokens ~ 0.2-0.4 h on one L40S ~ $0.2-0.5; at the bound (all 1,595, both candidates) ~ 9.7M prefill ~ $0.6. option_2_workbench.source: olly-styles/WorkBench@49c7dfd0 (MIT, (c) 2024 MindsDB): 690 tasks = 69 base templates x 10 (its generator's cap, seed 42), 5 sandbox databases, 26 tools; ground truth = the list of state-changing calls; graded by the sandbox's final state
option_2_workbench.schema_arguments_supply: under the frozen category rule (one call step with structured arguments) only 2 of 69 templates qualify -- direct analytics.create_plot requests whose arguments all come from the request (20 published tasks, ONE tool); every other template reads first (an id, an address, a value) and is multi_turn. New instances of the 2 templates are near-identical single-tool calls: volume, but almost no diversity
option_2_workbench.isolation: every WorkBench task is offered the same toolkit (its default --tool_selection all; the company directory is shared by every domain), so under the frozen environment rule it is ONE environment and ONE split: training with probability 0.87, state_eval 0.04. It cannot be counted on for state_eval -- the binding gap -- without changing the frozen atomic isolation
option_2_workbench.contamination: a published benchmark: regenerated instances share its templates, so WorkBench can never be a held-out evaluation afterwards; its 690 tasks excluded exactly and by 13-grams
option_2_workbench.verification: G1, final-state equality including side effects: the strongest of all candidates (for create_plot it amounts to an exact match of the arguments)
option_2_workbench.engineering: an executable backend in the episode loop (its pandas sandbox at the pinned commit, a state reset per episode, no network; it pins numpy<2, this venv has numpy 2.5.1: its own environment or a port), JSON schemas for its 26 Python tools, a port of its final-state grader, the generator run under new seeds with de-duplication, a converter and tests: days, not hours; generation itself is cheap
option_2_workbench.fills: H-N training only if its single environment hashes to training, and then with one tool; H-N state_eval: nothing expected

analysis.conclusion: For this gap option 1 is the stronger choice: it is the only one of the two that adds state-evaluation supply and it fills non-thinking training at the expected yield, at the same step-gold level as today's Pivot data minus recorded execution. Option 2 verifies more strongly but cannot supply state evaluation under the frozen isolation and supplies schema_arguments through one tool. Neither closes non-thinking state evaluation at the expected pass rate: with option 1 about 1,400 of 1,800 positions. Nothing is implemented or generated; the choice, and after the pilot's measured pass rate any SHORTFALL decision for that one cell, are the maintainer's
